title: Administrative Regulation on the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program Usage Fee: Posting, Meal-Status Waivers and Early-Return Credit
content:
## Section 1. Posting of the usage fee

1.1 Each of the six usage types carries its own usage fee and its own fee period, the school year or the summer, as its fee schedule states.

1.2 The usage fee of the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program posts on the checkout date at the usage fee of the usage type, or at the mid-year share of it for a school-year checkout on or after the mid-year start date.

1.3 The fee covers routine maintenance and the year-end cleaning when the usage type's fee schedule shows both as covered by the usage fee, and does not insure the instrument, as the schedule's insurance column shows.

1.4 The mid-year start date is read within the checkout's school year: it is the January date that falls inside that school year. A school-year checkout dated before it posts the full usage fee; one dated on it or after it posts the mid-year share. A Summer Instrument Checkout is not a school-year checkout and posts its usage fee for the summer.

## Section 2. Meal-status waivers

2.1 Waivers follow Texas Education Code 11.158 through the student's School Nutrition meal status on the posting date: the free meal waiver share as a free meal waiver credit for any Free Meal Status tier, the reduced meal waiver share as a reduced meal waiver credit for any Reduced-Price Meal Status tier, rounded to the nearest cent, half a cent rounding up.

2.2 The meal status that decides the waiver is the one the student holds on the date the usage fee posts, which is the checkout date. Every Free Meal Status tier earns the free meal waiver share, whatever its basis; every Reduced-Price Meal Status tier earns the reduced meal waiver share.

2.3 The waiver is a share of the usage fee as posted, and it is booked as a credit against that fee.

## Section 3. Early-return credit

3.1 An instrument turned in within the usage fee refund window of calendar days after checkout credits the usage type's early-return share of the fee net of waivers as an early return credit; later returns earn no credit.

3.2 The window is counted from the checkout date as day 0. A return on the last day of the window is inside it; a return on the day after is a later return and earns no credit.

## Worked examples on hypothetical figures

The rates in these examples are hypothetical and chosen to show the rounding and the order of the steps; the program's own figures are those of its fee schedule and rate table.

**Example A (mid-year date).** A hypothetical school-year usage type with a usage fee of 80.00 and a mid-year share of 50%. A checkout dated the day before the mid-year start date posts 80.00; a checkout dated on the mid-year start date posts 40.00.

**Example B (rounding).** A hypothetical posted usage fee of 62.75 and a hypothetical waiver share of 50%. Half of 62.75 is 31.375; rounded to the nearest cent with half a cent rounding up, the waiver credit is 31.38, leaving 31.37 net of waivers.

**Example C (early return).** Taking Example B's fee net of waivers of 31.37 and a hypothetical early-return share of 100% with a window of 10 days: a return on day 10 is credited 31.37 as an early return credit; a return on day 11 earns no credit.

## Points of judgement

- **Status changes after posting.** The waiver follows the meal status on the posting date, not a status the student holds later.
